_doc: Disc and block neodymium (NdFeB) magnets for printed parts: the sizes held, each with its seller's pull straight off thick steel and its grade, the remanence of each grade (to scale a pull to another grade), the size tolerance, the density, and the formula a pull across a gap is taken from. A magnet's pocket takes its fit from the printer's rules (x1c.magnet_press, x1c.magnet_glue, x1c.magnet_crush). Read by @rulecad/fixings' magnetModel. kind as in x1c.json.
name: magnets

disc_6x2_pull.rule: A 6 x 2 mm disc magnet of grade N45 pulls this hard, straight off, on a thick plate of mild steel it touches: the seller's adhesive force. Another grade is scaled from it by the square of its remanence; a gap or a thin steel strike takes less
disc_6x2_pull.source: supermagnete (Webcraft GmbH), disc magnet 6 x 2 mm, item S-06-02-N, N45, nickel-plated: adhesive force approx. 0.74 kg (approx. 7.26 N), 0.43 g, https://www.supermagnete.de/eng/disc-magnets-neodymium/disc-magnet-6mm-2mm_S-06-02-N

grade.rule: The grade a magnet is taken to be where its name gives none: N35, the commonest and weakest sold, so a pull is not overstated
grade.source: A working figure of @rulecad/fixings: N35 is the lowest grade the sellers list

tolerance.rule: A sintered disc or block magnet is within this of its nominal size, each way: so a press pocket is a close call and crush ribs take up the spread
tolerance.source: supermagnete S-08-03-N and ALB Materials D-D8H3-N35 both give a tolerance of ±0.1 mm, https://www.albmaterials.com/disc-magnets/3989-8mm-dia-x-3mm-thick-round-disc-magnets-d-d8h3-n35.html

density.rule: Density of sintered NdFeB, for a magnet's mass
density.source: Worked from sellers' weights: an 8 x 3 mm disc is 150.8 mm³ and weighs 1.131 g (ALB D-D8H3-N35) and 1.1 g (supermagnete S-08-03-N), 7.5 and 7.3 g/cm³

field_formula.rule: The flux density on the axis of a disc magnet, at z from its face (D its thickness, R its radius); a block's is Br/π [atan(LW / (2z sqrt(4z²+L²+W²))) - atan(LW / (2(D+z) sqrt(4(D+z)²+L²+W²)))]. The pull across a gap is taken as the pull touching times (B(z)/B(0))²: an estimate
field_formula.source: supermagnete FAQ, How do you calculate the magnetic flux density?, https://www.supermagnete.de/eng/faq/How-do-you-calculate-the-magnetic-flux-density (the formulas); the square from the force on an iron face, F = B² A / 2μ0, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Force_between_magnets (the approach, not the sellers' figures, which are measured)
